column1: # Campaign manifest for h200_campaign_queue.sh: EXP-R2-215 (D2.i), mode subspaces on the ProLLaMA lineage.
# Columns, tab-separated: slot <TAB> key <TAB> gpu <TAB> stage <TAB> label <TAB> env <TAB> args
# `--device` and `--out` are injected by the runner and must never appear in args.
# ${TRANSFER_MODEL_BASE_DIR} is substituted in-pod after h200_env.sh is sourced, so the model root stays declared once.
# ONE SNAPSHOT, key `d2i`. Every cell of this campaign is one comparison and must run one code hash.
# CARD 0 ONLY. This is one of three manifests -- cards 0, 1 and 3 -- frozen together and differing in nothing
# but the gpu column. The column is static and a manifest reaches the pod only inside a snapshot, so "dispatch
# onto the first card that frees" cannot be written as one file; it is written as one file per admissible card,
# with the dispatcher choosing at launch. THEY ARE ALTERNATIVES AND NOT PARALLEL LANES -- dispatch exactly
# ONE of the three. All three carry `--campaign campaign_d2i`, so the queue's per-campaign lock refuses a
# second live runner, and all three carry the same six labels, so a second runner under a different
# campaign name would write the same six cells into the same label-keyed output directories.
# CARD 2 IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: it reports one uncorrected volatile ECC
# error while the other three report zero, and this estimand is a difference between two forward passes read
# down to rank-1 ablations where the damages to be resolved are small -- the case where a single silently
# corrupted value is indistinguishable from a result rather than showing up as a crash. That is the same
# reasoning that put this stage in float32 rather than bfloat16.
# The queue REFUSES a busy card rather than waiting for it, which is what makes choosing a card at launch safe:
# losing a race costs a refusal and nothing else. All three manifests are dispatched with --campaign campaign_d2i
# so the status file is one observation channel whichever card is used, and a cell completed under one card is
# skipped by a re-dispatch under another -- the completion test is a *.json in the cell's own output directory,
# which is keyed by run id and label rather than by card.
# SLOTS 1-3 ARE THE FIRST DRAW AND 4-6 THE SECOND, in that order deliberately: an interrupted campaign then
# leaves a complete first draw rather than half of each. EXP-R2-215 freezes the second draw as mandatory
# (Appendix B rule 1), and 20260729 is the seed EXP-R2-152 re-drew this same lineage at, so the two draws are a
# second sample of one population rather than a second window of one permutation. --position-seed is held FIXED
# across the pair on purpose: with a different cohort the within-record draw is over different records anyway,
# and moving both would confound cohort sensitivity with position sensitivity.
# --batch-size 8 rather than the workstation smoke test's 4. It changes how records group into batches and
# therefore which positions the seeded per-batch draw selects, so it is part of a draw's identity and is held
# IDENTICAL across all six cells; it is not a free knob and must not be varied between the two draws.
# Llama-2-7b-hf enters with BOTH modes named. Its protein mode reads +0.0843 nats/token of context information
# and a reversal cost of -0.0013 nats/residue (EXP-R2-152, re-measured at EXP-R2-174), so its layers are
# expected to reach NO_MEASURED_DAMAGE, VOID_INSTRUMENT, UNIGRAM_ONLY or MIXED. That is decided by this
# stage's own measured residual damage under the decision rule, not in advance: the 0.30-nat pre-gate that
# used to refuse the mode by a declared number from another cohort is retired (L41, EXP-R2-218).
